title: One installation supplies the execution toolchain

nodes.summary: Installation bundles the full guest toolchain; runtime uses only it
nodes.detail: Installation provides the native kernel, pinned MicroHs compiler/evaluator, cpphs, base/SDK libraries, guest codecs, native libraries, web assets and notices. Runtime package compilation uses only these bundled tools and captured local source, never system Cabal resolution or a network download during validation.

realised.evidence: PR #44 stages the bundled runtime (GHC-built MicroHs as bin/mhs, evaluator, cpphs, SDK) used by the installed CLI journey; web assets absent

nodes.summary: Rerunnable agent-drivable installer with structured SetupReport and readiness check
nodes.detail: A bootstrap-supplied, safe-to-rerun install returns a SetupReport of installed components and outstanding requirements (missing component, permission, authentication, unsupported configuration), and a separate readiness/doctor operation runs an offline compile without provisioning. Permissions and human authentication surface as explicit needs-input, never silent privilege escalation.

realised.evidence: No SetupReport/readiness command in code; only the developer install-cli.sh exists (seq 46)

nodes.summary: Toolchain distribution is distinct from source-only tap plugin install
nodes.detail: Installing Kyyn may download verified pinned release artifacts, but tap plugins are vendored as source and compiled locally; no tap-supplied executables or plugin attestation service, and no plugin version pins or negotiation for the first release.

realised.evidence: PR #90 installs plugin source through the CLI, compiled locally with the bundled toolchain

deliveries.evidence: PR #89 vendors plugin source and origin into the KB through porcelain without executables; the CLI install route follows in #90

nodes.summary: GHC, C compiler and Node.js are build-time dependencies only
nodes.detail: Source and release builds may use GHC, a C compiler and Node.js, and generated scanners are release build inputs; none is required on an ordinary user's machine.

realised.evidence: PR #44: 'GHC is build-time only'; installed CLI runs KB code through bundled MicroHs

nodes.summary: Web UI ships as prebuilt static assets served natively
nodes.detail: Node.js tooling builds the Web UI into static browser assets packaged with Kyyn and served by the native application; the installed app needs no Node server, package manager or dev server.

realised.evidence: No web/ directory or asset build exists at end of history; seq 143 PR lists Web as desired, not available

nodes.summary: Bundled tools located by absolute path, not PATH mutation
nodes.detail: Bundled tools, including cpphs via MHSCPPHS, are invoked through absolute paths rather than requiring users to modify PATH.

realised.evidence: MHSCPPHS first used in code in PR #6 MicroHs integration

nodes.summary: Separate vendored source, disposable caches, secrets and authored files
nodes.detail: Vendored source and origins travel with the KB but generated executables do not. Build identity covers source, contract, compiler, options, SDK and dependencies, so a runtime version change invalidates binaries, never accepted facts, with no cross-version artifact portability claim.

realised.evidence: BuildIdentity from PR #8; per-KB disposable compiled-artifact cache keyed by build identity in PR #132; checkout-local secrets at seq 98

deliveries.evidence: PR #8 adds BuildIdentity over captured source, entry and pinned toolchain, with compiled artifacts held only in temporary scope; vendored packages, local secrets and the per-KB cache were still missing
PR #89 vendors plugin source with its origin into the KB's Git tree, with no executables
PR #122 keeps secrets checkout-local under ignored .kyyn/secrets; the disposable per-KB compiled-artifact cache keyed by build identity follows in #132

nodes.summary: Git plumbing via a tested Git executable behind a capability
nodes.detail: Canonical Git operations go through a Git executable behind the Git capability rather than a libgit2 binding, and missing Git is an actionable installation requirement; bundling versus locating Git is unsettled.

realised.evidence: PR #20 implements the read-only Git boundary through the Git executable (GitUnavailable diagnostic); write side in PR #23

nodes.summary: Staged compiler is the GHC-built pinned MicroHs
nodes.detail: The bundled compiler is the pinned MicroHs built with GHC; GHC is needed to build it, not to execute KB code. Native library dependencies and notices still need distribution review.

realised.evidence: PR #44 stages the upstream GHC-built MicroHs compiler under bin/mhs

nodes.summary: Development install deploys kyyn-v2 bundle and resolves symlinked runtime
nodes.detail: A source-build convenience installs the staged bundle under PREFIX/lib/kyyn-v2 and links bin/kyyn-v2, temporarily named to coexist with v1. Runtime discovery canonicalises the link to find bundled assets. It is explicitly not the cross-platform release installer.

realised.evidence: PR #49 adds tools/install-cli.sh and canonicalised executable-path runtime discovery

nodes.summary: SDK edit dependencies ship as vendored transformers source subset
nodes.detail: The guest SDK's fact-editing dependencies ship as an unmodified, licensed transformers source subset with compiler-selected CPP branches, so users never install another package manager or fetch libraries to edit facts.

realised.evidence: PR #64 stages the unmodified transformers subset with its license in vendor/

editorial.note: Also converts status line to front-matter metadata and basis statement
Repoints install-command ownership from docs/cli-development.md to the user guide and staging script
Desired-state reconciliation: removes status/date/basis, rephrases the distribution-review caveat and drops 'exact command names are illustrative'; no new requirement

notes: This ADR is about distribution, and it remains mostly aspirational. The parts that sit inside the dev loop are real: bundled MicroHs/cpphs (built at 43), Git via executable (19), build identity and per-KB caches (8, 104) and vendored transformers (55). The user-facing promises are all unrealised: the SetupReport/readiness installer, Web assets and cross-platform/WSL release proof. The only installer that exists is the kyyn-v2 developer script (seq 46), and the ADR is careful to say it is not the release installer. The founding Decision has no subsections, so I split it into 8 commitments. I kept 'build tools are build-time only' (0020.04) separate from 'Web as static assets' (0020.05) because one is realised and the other is not. 0020.03 overlaps ADR 0015's plugin-install decision, and I dated it by the first source-plugin install.
